mainEntity.name: What is a safe way to clean an acrylic denture at home?

acceptedAnswer.text: A generally safe approach is to use a soft-bristled denture brush alongside a specialist denture cleaning paste or gel, which is formulated to be gentle on acrylic materials. Soaking the denture in an effervescent denture cleansing solution can also help reduce microbial build-up between brushing sessions. Rinsing the denture under cool water after meals helps remove loose debris. Avoid very hot water and standard toothpastes, as these can damage the acrylic surface or distort the denture's shape over time.

mainEntity.name: Can whitening toothpaste be used on a denture?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Whitening toothpastes typically contain higher concentrations of abrasive particles and may include bleaching agents. Both components can be damaging to acrylic denture surfaces, accelerating surface scratching and potentially affecting the colour and structural integrity of the material. If discolouration of your denture is a concern, speak with your dentist, who may be able to advise on appropriate professional cleaning or discuss whether the denture requires replacement or refurbishment.

mainEntity.name: How often should I clean my denture?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most dental professionals recommend cleaning your denture at least once daily, typically in the evening before removing it overnight. Rinsing the denture after meals is also advisable to remove food debris. Overnight soaking in an appropriate cleansing solution helps maintain hygiene between brushing sessions. Your dentist may recommend a specific routine based on your individual circumstances, denture type, and oral health.

mainEntity.name: Why does my denture still smell even after cleaning?

acceptedAnswer.text: Persistent odour despite regular cleaning may indicate that bacteria or fungi are colonising microscopic surface scratches on the denture. This can occur if abrasive products have been used over a period of time. It may also suggest that the cleaning routine is not fully disrupting the biofilm on the denture surface, or that the denture requires a professional clean. If the issue persists, it is worth raising with your dentist, as they can assess both the denture and the underlying oral tissues.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to leave my denture in water overnight?

acceptedAnswer.text: For many patients, storing the denture in clean cool water overnight is appropriate and helps prevent the acrylic from drying out and potentially distorting. Some clinicians recommend using a denture soaking solution for additional antimicrobial benefit. However, the most appropriate storage method may vary depending on your specific denture type and the materials used in its construction. Your dentist can provide advice on this question for your individual situation.

mainEntity.name: How often should I see a dentist if I wear a full denture?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dental reviews remain important even when all natural teeth have been replaced. The oral soft tissues, bone structure, and the condition and fit of the denture should all be assessed periodically. Over time, changes in the underlying bone and gum tissue can affect denture fit. Many dental professionals recommend an annual review as a general guide, though individual needs may vary. Your dentist will advise on the frequency most appropriate for you.
